title: The Empty Alibi
premise: When the coffin of town founder Abigail Marsh is exhumed for a cemetery relocation and found empty, concierge Felix Underhill realizes the guest registers, letters, and gossip she has quietly archived for twelve years hold the key to a thirty-year-old disappearance. As Felix follows a trail of forged alibis through the town's founding families, she discovers Abigail never died — she fled after witnessing something terrible, and someone in town has been paying to keep that secret buried. The killer, now elderly and desperate, begins destroying evidence and threatening witnesses, forcing Felix to choose between protecting her loyal patrons and exposing the truth. In the end, Felix finds Abigail alive in hiding, confronts the murderer at the old Marsh estate, and lets the law take him — but chooses to keep one merciful secret of her own.
about_author: Wendell Coldharbour spent two decades working night desks at grand hotels before turning to crime fiction, claiming the lobby is where every town's secrets check in. He lives in a converted coach house and writes only between midnight and dawn.

chapters.title: The Guest Who Never Left
chapters.summary: Felix Underhill's POV. During a routine cemetery relocation, workers open Abigail Marsh's coffin and find it empty. Felix, watching from the crowd, recognizes the undertaker's flinch — a man who stayed at her hotel last week. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath professional composure.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Keys
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. She reviews her private archive of guest ledgers and finds the undertaker checked in under a false name, paid cash, and made one call to the Marsh estate. Her manager warns her to stay out of it. Beat: loyalty to the hotel tested against curiosity.

chapters.title: A Town Built on One Name
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Researching Abigail Marsh's history, Felix learns the founder 'died' thirty years ago, yet no death certificate exists — only a burial permit signed by the current mayor's father. Beat: the first crack in the town's polished story.

chapters.title: The Undertaker Checks Out
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Before Felix can question him, the undertaker is found dead in his bathtub, ruled accidental. A matchbook from the Marsh estate sits on his sink. Beat: fear arrives; this is no longer a puzzle but a hunt.

chapters.title: Alibi, Thirty Years Old
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. She interviews three aging founding-family members who all claim they saw Abigail the night she supposedly died — at three different places. Their stories are rehearsed, word for word. Beat: the thrill of catching liars curdling into unease.

chapters.title: Room 214 Keeps Its Silence
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A retired journalist staying at the hotel admits he investigated Abigail's disappearance decades ago and was bought off. He gives Felix his old notes, then checks out before dawn. Beat: an ally gained and immediately lost.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Remembers
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Cross-referencing old hotel registers, Felix finds Abigail herself stayed at the hotel under an alias six months after her 'death' — and received weekly letters ever since, held at the front desk. Beat: hope; the founder may be alive.

chapters.title: The Mayor's Polished Shoes
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Mayor Edwin Marsh, Abigail's grandnephew, invites Felix to lunch and gently threatens her job, her lease, her reputation. His alibi for the exhumation week is flawless — too flawless. Beat: power pressing down; isolation deepens.

chapters.title: Letters Held at the Desk
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. She steals into the hotel's dead-letter cabinet and finds twenty-six unopened letters addressed to a Miss Vell. The handwriting is Abigail Marsh's. The most recent was collected yesterday — by someone still living. Beat: breathless discovery.

chapters.title: The Housekeeper's Confession
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: elderly housekeeper Ruth Okafor. Ruth reveals she has delivered money to 'Miss Vell' monthly for thirty years, ordered by the late patriarch — and that last week someone followed her home. Beat: guilt and terror of a lifelong accomplice.

chapters.title: Someone Is Editing the Past
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The hotel archives are ransacked; pages torn from the old registers. Felix's backup copies, hidden in plain sight as 'inventory records,' survive. Beat: violation and resolve — she is now the only witness.

chapters.title: The Night Abigail Ran
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Reconstructing from the journalist's notes, Felix pieces together the original crime: Abigail witnessed the patriarch kill a business partner and bury him beneath the estate's boathouse. Beat: horror reframing everything — the empty coffin was mercy, not mystery.

chapters.title: An Alibi Woven Twice
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix realizes the three founding families' matching alibis were coached by the same person — the man now mayor. The pattern of payments traces to a shell company Edwin controls. Beat: cold clarity; the heir inherited both fortune and cover-up.

chapters.title: Threats at the Front Desk
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Anonymous notes appear in Felix's mail slot; her tires are slashed; a guest she trusts asks pointed questions about her archive. Beat: paranoia — everyone in the lobby could be watching for someone else.

chapters.title: Ruth Disappears
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Ruth Okafor vanishes, leaving behind her delivery ledger and a note: 'Boathouse. She waits on Thursdays.' Beat: grief and urgency — the clock is now measured in lives.

chapters.title: Thursday at the Boathouse
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix stakes out the ruined Marsh boathouse and glimpses an old woman leaving flowers at a fresh concrete patch — Abigail, alive, mourning the partner whose body lies beneath. Beat: awe and heartbreak; the myth made flesh.

chapters.title: The Founder's Testimony
chapters.summary: Abigail's POV. Abigail tells Felix why she ran: no one would believe the town's beloved patriarch was a murderer, and staying meant death. She has watched the town flourish on a lie for thirty years. Beat: weary dignity; truth as exile.

chapters.title: Edwin Closes the Net
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Edwin learns Felix has found Abigail; he burns the estate's records and arranges an 'accident' at the hotel. Felix evacuates guests and hides Abigail in plain sight as an ordinary elderly visitor. Beat: siege; the concierge's skills weaponized for protection.

chapters.title: The Confession Recorded
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Using the hotel's ancient intercom system, Felix lures Edwin into repeating his great-uncle's crime aloud while Abigail listens from the switchboard room, recorded on the journalist's restored tapes. Beat: trap sprung; nerve and craft over force.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Edwin, cornered, offers Felix money, then violence; police arrive tipped by Ruth, found alive and hiding in the chapel. Edwin is arrested for two murders spanning thirty years. Beat: catharsis — the law finally works because Felix bent every rule to feed it.

chapters.title: What Felix Files Away
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. In the aftermath, the town reels; Felix declines interviews and quietly returns the stolen letters to Abigail, keeping only one page as insurance. Beat: bittersweet reflection on the cost of knowing everyone's secrets.

chapters.title: Checkout Time
chapters.summary: Abigail's POV, closing. Abigail, legally resurrected, checks into the hotel under her own name at last. Felix hands her the key to Room 214 — the room she once took under an alias. Beat: grace; a woman and a town finally allowed to remember honestly.
